You use the word "hate" many times, you seem to be very emotional, angry, etc

Could I suggest approaching things from a different angle

I used to be extremely angry and frustrated at politicians, at politics in general, the status quo, the poverty in the world, etc, etc.. everything annoyed me. I just dealt with it by moving abroad, and then I just ignored it. At some point, I got really big into World War 2, I couldn't stop consuming books on it.. and from there I kinda built an interest in history.. then sociology.. basically human development.. no agendas, narratives, just pure facts over fiction..

I also had a stint in a poor country where I experienced a good deal of genuine non-first-world-problems hardship

It's difficult for some of us to have a concept of what the world was like 25 years ago, 50 years ago.. how far we've come.. I've never experienced bread queues, I've never had the stress of being informed on by neighbours to internal security, nobody in my family has been stripped of citizenship, I've never gone through horrendous social strife, never experienced war, infectious diseases, conscription, living under a dictatorship, never had to pay off police.. I grew up relatively poor, but I've never experienced any of those things..

My "poor" childhood was infinitely better than those of generations before me

It's almost like we're so busy being "angry" and complaining that we completely take for granted what we have. Don't get me wrong, there's a hell of a lot that needs to be fixed, make no mistake about that.. but having no knowledge of how we got here, what we went through to get here.. it means the present makes less sense to us

I don't live in the States, I am in Europe.. and just over the last few generations, healthcare has increased, educational opportunites and options have improved, job mobility, job security, equality for women, rights in the work place, rights in general, health and safety, social welfare, infrastructure improvement, insurance.. living standards are constantly rising, illiteracy is dropping, infant mortality is dropping, environmental improvements, mental health issues improving, gay and lesbian recognition, we've living longer.. there are sub-Saharan African countries with access to the same technology, but they live like we did 200 years ago, with the same mentality. Even so, speaking of Africa, extreme poverty in the world has more than halved in the last 30 years

It's easy to lose perspective and to focus solely on the negative whilst ignoring the progress

A psychologist in the UK devised a system of tests to get people to gauge their views of the world. Just a series of questions. That particular test proved one thing conclusively - we have a psychological tendency to focus on the negative. One newspaper in Russia experimented by printing only good news, no bad news whatsoever, the result? readership plummeted

Many of us almost need to complain, to blame, to be angry - and that's nothing to do with Trump/Hillary/Iraq/politics... it's to do with psychology

You are living in the best time to be alive (presuming you are in a first world country), without repeating myself, you have more options and opportunities, fairness, rights and safety nets available to you than almost any time in history

It's perfectly fine to be frustrated, but I do recommend, if it's getting to you, delve into history a bit (only if it interests you) For very light and super interesting reading I recommend Bill Bryson - At Home. It's a history of everything we have in the house, but it builds an incredible perspective on history in general Also Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind by Harari

Even if you are not keen on sociology, anthropology - these books contain FACTS, not OPINIONS

There's no agenda, no narrative... I just find it's nice to lean back and get a perspective on everything, good luck
